| 1 | — | 1 |
| 4 | 4²=16, 4³=19, 4⁴=31, 4⁵=34, 4⁶=1 | 6 |
| 11 | 11²=31, 11³=26, 11⁴=16, 11⁵=41, 11⁶=1 | 6 |
| 14 | 14²=16, 14³=44, 14⁴=31, 14⁵=29, 14⁶=1 | 6 |
| 16 | 16²=31, 16³=1 | 3 |
| 19 | 19²=1 | 2 |
| 26 | 26²=1 | 2 |
| 29 | 29²=31, 29³=44, 29⁴=16, 29⁵=14, 29⁶=1 | 6 |
| 31 | 31²=16, 31³=1 | 3 |
| 34 | 34²=31, 34³=19, 34⁴=16, 34⁵=4, 34⁶=1 | 6 |
| 41 | 41²=16, 41³=26, 41⁴=31, 41⁵=11, 41⁶=1 | 6 |
| 44 | 44²=1 | 2 |

The maximum element order is 6, so **no element has order 12**. Therefore G is not cyclic, ruling out Z₁₂. Hence:

$$G \cong \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_3.$$

Each factor Z₂, Z₂, Z₃ is cyclic of prime-power order (2, 2, 3 are primes). Thus:

$$G \cong \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_3.$$

- ⟨19⟩ = {1, 19}
- ⟨26⟩ = {1, 26}
- ⟨44⟩ = {1, 44}

The elements of order 3 are 16, 31, giving one subgroup of order 3:
- ⟨16⟩ = {1, 16, 31}

Select H₁ = ⟨19⟩, H₂ = ⟨26⟩, H₃ = ⟨16⟩. These are cyclic of prime-power order (2, 2, 3 respectively). They pairwise intersect trivially (any two distinct order-2 subgroups share only {1}; the order-3 subgroup shares only {1} with any order-2 subgroup since gcd(2,3)=1). The product has size 2·2·3 = 12 = |G|.

**Verification that H₁H₂H₃ = G** — listing all 12 products mod 45:

| | 1 | 16 | 31 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1·1 | 1 | 16 | 31 |
| 1·26 | 26 | 11 | 41 |
| 19·1 | 19 | 34 | 4 |
| 19·26 | 44 | 29 | 14 |

This yields {1, 4, 11, 14, 16, 19, 26, 29, 31, 34, 41, 44} = G. ✓

Therefore:

$$G = \langle 19 \rangle \times \langle 26 \rangle \times \langle 16 \rangle = \{1,19\} \times \{1,26\} \times \{1,16,31\}$$

is the internal direct product, where ⟨19⟩ ≅ Z₂, ⟨26⟩ ≅ Z₂, ⟨16⟩ ≅ Z₃.
